## Introduction — The Multimodal Imperative


**Historical Challenge**

- Early nCT/nCRT regimens: high toxicity, treatment-related mortality, marginal survival benefit
- Over 40 years of evolution driven by better understanding of **tumor histology and biology**

**Core Principle**

- Multiple RCTs: nCT or nCRT confers better survival vs surgery alone
- Controls **local** and **micrometastatic** disease
- Majority of patients ultimately die of recurrence

## Introduction — The Multimodal Imperative

**Current Landscape**

- Ideal regimen still not fully elucidated
- Immunotherapy role yet to be clearly defined
- **Surgical standard:** Transthoracic *en bloc* esophagogastrectomy + extended lymphadenectomy
  - Highest R0 resection rate
  - Lowest locoregional recurrence

**Chapter Focus**

- Evolution of neoadjuvant treatments
- Evidence base for treatment decisions
- Future trends in management


---

## Neoadjuvant Radiotherapy (nRT) vs Surgery Alone

**Historical Context**

- First studies: 1950s, primarily ESCC
- Goal: local disease response + R0 resection
- 5-year OS: only **6–10%** — minimal benefit over surgery alone

**Cochrane Review (5 trials, n = 1147)**

- Majority ESCC
- Absolute survival benefit: **only 4% at 5 years** vs surgery alone
- Failed to reach statistical significance
- nRT dose considerably lower than modern regimens
- Did not combine nRT with concurrent chemotherapy


## Neoadjuvant Radiotherapy (nRT) vs Surgery Alone

**Higher-Dose nRT — Still Insufficient**

- Even higher doses of nRT alone fail to achieve meaningful survival improvement
- Chinese multiarm study (40 Gy nRT vs surgery):
  - Improved **3-year** OS with nRT
  - Not sustained at **5 years**



**Conclusion:** nRT alone is **not** an accepted standard of care for locally advanced esophageal cancer. Its use as a solitary treatment strategy should remain in the **palliative** realm.


## Neoadjuvant Chemoradiotherapy (nCRT) — Rationale

**Rationale for Adding Chemotherapy to RT**

- Systemic treatment extends efficacy to **micrometastatic disease** beyond the radiation field
- Several agents act as **radiosensitizers**:
  - 5-FU
  - Cisplatin
  - Paclitaxel


**Histological Sensitivity**

- ESCC is **particularly sensitive** to radiotherapy
- EAC has more attenuated response
- This difference drives histology-specific treatment decisions


**Meta-analysis of 26 early studies (n = 1335)**

- pCR achieved in **24%** of patients
- Dose-related response confirmed
- Role of combined systemic treatment formalized

**Early Toxicity Challenges**

- 64.8 Gy nCRT → **9%** treatment-related deaths
- Cisplatin/vinblastine/5FU (Forastiere 1990) → grade III–IV myelosuppression in **93%**
- Bosset et al.: nCRT deaths significantly higher than post-surgery

## The CROSS Trial — Landmark Evidence


**Design (van Hagen et al., 2012; n = 366)**

- Regimen: **Carboplatin + Paclitaxel + 41.4 Gy**
- Mixed histology: EAC & ESCC

**Key Pathological Outcomes**

- pCR: 25% (EAC) vs **49%** (ESCC)
- R0 resection: **92%** (nCRT) vs 69% (surgery)
- Nodal positivity: 31% (nCRT) vs 75% (surgery)
- Locoregional recurrence: **22%** vs 38% (HR 0.45, P <0.001)


**Survival (Long-term follow-up, median 45 months)**

- Median OS: **48.6 mo** (nCRT) vs 24.0 mo (surgery), P = 0.003
- ESCC median OS: **81.6 months**
- EAC median OS: 43.2 months



The CROSS trial **firmly established** nCRT as standard of care for both ESCC and EAC in the West



**Caveat on Surgical Approach**

- Dutch CROSS data: persistent chemoradiation benefit with transhiatal resection but **limited benefit** with transthoracic esophagectomy — raising questions about necessity of nCRT when en bloc surgery is performed




## nCRT vs Surgery — Key Trial Findings: EAC


**Walsh et al. (1996) — EAC, n = 113**

- 5FU + cisplatin + 40 Gy vs surgery alone
- pCR: 25%; nodal positivity: 42% vs 82%
- 3-yr OS: **32%** vs 6%
- *Caveat: surgery alone arm OS far below contemporary benchmarks*

**Tepper et al. (2008) — 77% EAC, n = 56**

- Cisplatin + 5FU + 50.4 Gy
- 5-yr OS: **39%** (nCRT) vs 16% (surgery)


**FFCD 9901 (Mariette, 2014) — 70% ESCC, Stage I/II only**

- No significant difference in R0 or 3-yr OS
- **6× increase** in postoperative mortality in radiated arm
- Interpretation: unsuitability of trimodal therapy in **early-stage** ESCC

**NEOCRTEC5010 (Yang, 2018) — ESCC, n = 451**

- Vinorelbine + cisplatin + 40 Gy
- pCR: 43.2%; R0: 98.4% vs 91.2%
- Median OS: **100.1** vs 66.5 months (P = 0.002)
- 5-yr OS: 59.1% (trimodal) vs 49.1% (surgery) — better than CROSS


## Role of nCRT in Systemic Control


**Locoregional vs Distant Recurrence**

- Retrospective study (n = 204): nCRT vs surgery
  - Locoregional recurrence: **12% vs 28%** (P = 0.001)
  - Distal recurrence: 25% vs 35% (P = .210) — *not significant*
- Burmeister et al.: 5-yr PFS improved with nCRT in **ESCC** but **not** EAC
- Lv et al. (ESCC): systemic recurrence death — surgery 38.8% vs nCRT 25.0% (P = .011)

**CROSS Recurrence Data**

- Clear locoregional benefit from nCRT
- **No reduction** in distant disease relapse for whole cohort
- ESCC subset: some systemic benefit at 5 years (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.56–1.01)


**Impact of Pathological Complete Response**

*Multicenter study (n = 895, median follow-up 52.9 months)*

| Scenario | ESCC Recurrence | EAC Recurrence |
|---|---|---|
| **pCR achieved** | 21% | 24% |
| — Locoregional | 4.3% | 14.0% |
| — Distal | 1.7% | 17.4% |
| **No pCR** | 56% | 50% |

- ESCC: equal locoregional & distal recurrence (16.7% vs 17.5%)
- EAC: predominantly **distal** recurrence (32.5% vs 6.3% locoregional)
- After pCR: locoregional recurrence 6%, distant mets 26%



nCRT provides excellent **local** control when pCR achieved; when not — both local and distal control are suboptimal, especially in EAC






## nCRT in Early-Stage Esophageal Cancer


**FFCD 9901 — Stage I & II (Mariette et al., n = 195)**

- 5FU + cisplatin + 45 Gy vs transthoracic surgery
- R0 resection: comparable (92.9% vs 92.1%)
- pCR: 33% in nCRT group
- Local failure: **28.6%** (nCRT) vs **44.3%** (surgery), P = .02
- Distant recurrence: **no difference** (22.5% vs 28.9%)
- Overall survival: **no difference** (31.8 vs 41.1 months)
- In-hospital mortality: **11.1%** (nCRT) vs 3.4% (surgery), P = .049



Oncologic benefit of nCRT in locally advanced disease **not maintained** in early-stage disease


**cT3N0 Retrospective Study (30 European centers, n = 382)**

- Addition of neoadjuvant treatment → more R0 resections, fewer positive nodes, more downstaging, longer OS (38.4 vs 29.9 months, P = .007)
- Outcomes did **not differ** between nCRT vs nCT

**Definitive CRT Without Surgery in ESCC?**

- ESCC highly sensitive to RT — surgery necessity questioned
- Registry study (n = 3123, stage I–III): adding surgery to nCRT → survival benefit, but only from **stage IIA** upward
- JCOG0502 (cT1bN0): 5-yr OS similar — surgery vs definitive CRT (86.5% vs 85.5%)
- Multiple ongoing trials addressing selective surgery after induction CRT — results anticipated mid-2020s



## Balancing Toxicity and Benefit of nCRT


**Preoperative Toxicity**

- Bone marrow suppression
- Nutritional depletion
- Renal damage
- Liver damage

*Early concern (Bosset et al.):* nCRT mortality negated survival benefit — but split-dose radiation now known to be deleterious

**Modern nCRT Safety Data**

- Treatment-related deaths: **<2%** in recent studies
- CROSS: most common — leukopenia, neutropenia, anorexia, fatigue (2–6%); only 1/176 deaths awaiting surgery
- NEOCRTEC5010: treatment-associated mortality **1.3%**


**Postoperative Morbidity**

*Multi-institutional study (n = 2944):* nCRT **not** associated with:
- ↑ Anastomotic leak
- ↑ Pneumonia
- ↑ Overall morbidity/mortality

But nCRT **was** associated with:
- ↑ Chylothorax (2.5% vs 0.2%, P = .020)
- ↑ Cardiovascular complications (8.6% vs 0.1%, P = .037)
- ↑ Thromboembolic events (8.6% vs 6.0%, P = .037)

**Meta-analysis (12 RCTs, n = 1529):**  
No increase in postoperative morbidity (RR 0.97) or mortality (RR 0.56)

**Recommendation:** Reserve nCRT for **locally advanced** disease; role in early-stage disease remains unclear


## The Case for Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy (nCT)


**Rationale for nCT**

1. Controls **occult distant/micrometastatic** disease
2. Improves dysphagia → better nutrition pre-surgery
3. Downstaging of non-resectable lesions
4. Optimal drug delivery via intact blood supply
5. **Assesses in-vivo tumor response** — guides further therapy
6. Avoids futile surgery if disease progresses

**Early Negative Studies**

- *Kelsen et al. (Intergroup 0113):* Cisplatin + 5FU — no OS benefit vs surgery alone
- *Subset:* Responders had markedly better survival (HR 2.83, P <0.001)
- *Schlag et al. (ESCC):* No OS benefit overall, but **responders** — median OS 42.2 vs 13.8 months
- *Ancona et al. (ESCC):* No ITT benefit; but in **40% major responders** — median OS 53 months, 5-yr OS 60%


**Positive Pivotal Studies**

**MRC OEO2 (n = 802, EAC + ESCC)**

- Cisplatin + 5FU vs surgery alone
- 2-yr OS: 34% → **43%**; 5-yr OS: 17% → **23%**
- HR 0.79 (95% CI 0.67–0.93, P = .004)
- Established nCT as standard for locally advanced EAC
- Long-term follow-up: EAC slightly greater benefit than ESCC

**MAGIC Trial (n = 503, predominantly EAC)**

- ECF (epirubicin, cisplatin, 5FU) perioperative
- R0: 79.3% vs 70.3% (P = .03)
- Smaller tumors, less advanced nodal disease
- 5-yr OS: **36.3%** vs 23% (HR 0.75, P = .009)
- *Only 55% received postoperative therapy*

**FNLCC/FFCD (cisplatin + 5FU, 75% lower esophageal/junction)**

- Comparable survival outcomes to MAGIC

## The Dawn of the Docetaxel Era — EAC

**Background**

- Earlier studies: doublet regimens (platinum + 5FU)
- MAGIC: added anthracycline (triplet) → further survival gain
- Observation: metastatic gastric Ca responds well to docetaxel-based triplet therapy

**DCF (Docetaxel + Cisplatin + 5FU)**

- Phase II (Ferri et al.): perioperative DCF for EAC
- Exceptional **5-yr OS >50%** despite heavy tumor burden

**FLOT4 Trial (Al-Batran et al., 2019, n = 716)**

- **FLOT** (5FU + leucovorin + oxaliplatin + docetaxel) vs ECF (MAGIC regimen)
- Median OS: 35 → **50 months**
- Equivalent toxicity and postoperative complications
- Validated in real-world RealFLOT study (n = 206)


**FLOT Extended to True EAC**

- FLOT4 included type II esophagogastric junction — excluded type I/true EAC
- Genomic analysis: proximal gastric & EAC are **almost identical** — should be treated as single disease (gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma)
- Multicenter observational cohort (3 high-volume centers): FLOT4 results **extrapolate** to EAC patients
- Neoadjuvant FLOT + en bloc transthoracic surgery → **5-yr OS 60%** despite disease burden



**Docetaxel-based nCT is now the standard of care for resectable locally advanced EAC**


## The Dawn of the Docetaxel Era — ESCC


**Cisplatin + 5FU Established in ESCC**

- JCOG 9204 (Ando et al.): cisplatin + 5FU → survival benefit in **adjuvant** setting for stage II/III ESCC
- JCOG 9907: **neoadjuvant** CF superior to adjuvant CF
  - 5-yr OS improved by 12% → **55%**
  - But: concerns about undertreatment and high early postoperative recurrence


**Adding Docetaxel — DCF vs CF in ESCC**

**NExT Trial (preliminary results)**

- DCF vs CF alone: 3-yr OS **72.1% vs 62.6%** — significant improvement

**Retrospective data**

- DCF vs CF: 3-yr OS **79% vs 65%** (P <0.05)

**Real-world data (n = 2148)**

- DCF vs CF: significantly longer OS (HR 0.868, 95% CI 0.770–0.978, P = .002)
- **No increase** in treatment/postoperative morbidity or mortality

**Randomized multicentric study**

- Adding Adriamycin to CF → still inferior to **docetaxel-based triplet**



For ESCC: nCT provides an effective alternative to nCRT, with docetaxel-based triplets leading outcomes




## nCT vs nCRT — Evidence in ESCC


**Key Debate**

- nCRT proponents: higher R0 + pCR rates
- nCT proponents: similar survival; chemotherapy in nCRT may itself control disease beyond radiation field

**RCT (Wang et al., 2021 — ESCC, n = 264)**

- nCRT (40 Gy + paclitaxel/cisplatin) vs nCT (paclitaxel + cisplatin)
- Fewer cancer-related deaths with nCRT
- 3-yr OS: **64% vs 55%** — *not statistically significant*
- pCR higher in nCRT; trend to lower recurrence (38% vs 49%, P = .062)

**Chinese 4-arm study (nCT / nCRT / surgery / nRT)**

- All neoadjuvant therapies improved 3-yr OS
- At **5 years**: nCT and nCRT had **similar outcomes**


**NExT Trial (Kato et al., n = 601)**

- 200 patients: nCRT arm (CF + 41.4 Gy)
- nCRT median OS: **6.0 years** — did not differ from nCT arms
- Despite PFS longer in nCRT (5.3 vs 2.7 years)
- Treatment-related deaths similar (1.0–2.0%)

**Retrospective support**

- Multiple propensity-matched studies confirm **non-inferiority** of nCRT over nCT
- Differing chemotherapy regimens within nCRT do not significantly affect ESCC survival


For ESCC: **Both nCT and nCRT are accepted standards of care**. nCRT achieves better locoregional control; nCT achieves equivalent overall survival.


## nCT vs nCRT — Evidence in EAC


**POET Trial (Stahl et al., n = 119, Siewert I–III adenocarcinoma)**

- nCRT vs nCT; 3- and 5-yr OS: 46.7%/39.5% (nCRT) vs 26.1%/24.4% (nCT)
- Suggests nCRT superiority — but nCT arm OS lower than expected with modern regimens
- Only 47% in nCT arm had transthoracic esophagectomy — confounding surgical approach

**NeoRes Trial (Klevebro, n = 181 — EAC & ESCC)**

- nCRT vs nCT (CF ± 40 Gy)
- Higher pCR and R0 with radiation — but **no survival difference**
- Trend: EAC → better with nCT; ESCC → slightly better with nCRT
- Long-term 2019 results: 42.2% vs 39.6% (P = 0.60)
- Limitations: underpowered for subset analysis; low RT dose; non-standard chemotherapy


**NeoAEGIS Trial (Reynolds et al., n = 362 — adenocarcinoma)**

- CROSS vs MAGIC/ECF (± FLOT in latter phase)
- 3-yr OS: **57% vs 55%** (HR 1.03, 95% CI 0.77–1.38) — *no inferiority*
- FLOT only 15% of nCT cohort — potentially underestimating nCT arm performance

**ESOPEC Trial**

- Comparing FLOT vs CROSS for EAC — results awaited

**Summary for EAC**

- nCT is at least **non-inferior** to nCRT
- When pCR achieved after nCRT, survival still inferior vs nCT pCR (OR 2.50, P <0.05) → systemic control > local control for survival
- Population-based study (n = 11,167 EAC + 2367 ESCC): 5-yr OS similar overall (37% nCRT vs 36% nCT); ESCC significantly better with nCRT (45% vs 38%, P = .026)

## Safety — nCT vs nCRT


**Postoperative Mortality — Historical Data**

- Stahl et al. & Bedenne et al.: perioperative mortality **9–12%** with nCRT + surgery
- Stahl: nCRT mortality 9% vs nCT **3.8%** — higher but not statistically significant

**Modern Minimally Invasive Data**

- 2021 prospective multicenter RCT (minimally invasive esophagectomy):
  - Postoperative morbidity: 47.4% (nCRT) vs 42.6% (nCT)
  - Postoperative mortality: 3.5% vs 2.8%
  - **No significant difference**


**NeoAEGIS Safety Data**

- Similar overall safety profile
- But: significantly more patients on nCRT had **Clavien-Dindo grade III+** complications (30% vs 17%, P = .05)
- Higher mean **comprehensive complication index** with nCRT

**Meta-analysis (2022, n = 3137 ESCC patients, 18 studies)**

- nCRT vs nCT: **no difference** in incidence of postoperative complications



nCRT and nCT have broadly comparable safety in modern series, though nCRT may be associated with higher-grade complications in some studies



## Immunotherapy and Biological Agents


**HER2 — Trastuzumab**

- ToGA study: trastuzumab + CF in **HER2-positive advanced** gastric adenocarcinoma → median OS 11.1 → **13.5 months**
- NRG Oncology/RTOG 1010 (resectable EAC, HER2+):
  - Added trastuzumab to cisplatin + paclitaxel + 50.5 Gy → surgery
  - **No survival benefit**
  - Treatment-related deaths: 6% (trastuzumab) vs 3% (no trastuzumab)

**PD-1/PD-L1 Inhibitors**

- **KEYNOTE-590**: pembrolizumab + CF vs CF alone for advanced/metastatic esophageal cancer → improved OS, equivalent safety
- Preliminary data: preoperative pembrolizumab and nivolumab independently **increase tumoral response** to neoadjuvant therapy (survival data pending)


**Ongoing Trials**

- Neoadjuvant **pembrolizumab** + nCRT/nCT
- Neoadjuvant **avelumab** + perioperative chemotherapy (phase II — preliminary results)
- **ESONICT-2**: Toripalimab + docetaxel + cisplatin for ESCC
  - Major pathological response: **41.7%**
  - Survival data pending

**Safety of Immunotherapy + nCT**

- Several authors confirm immunotherapy **safe** when added concurrently with nCT — no increase in postoperative morbidity or mortality



**Current limitation:** Paucity of survival outcome data for neoadjuvant immunotherapy. Recommendations cannot yet be made for routine use — prospective trial results awaited.


## Summary — Histology-Guided Treatment Strategy


### Esophageal Adenocarcinoma (EAC)

- **Standard of care:** Docetaxel-based perioperative chemotherapy (FLOT) + en bloc surgery
- nCRT is at least non-inferior but not clearly superior
- FLOT → 5-yr OS **~60%** when combined with en bloc resection
- ESOPEC, TOPGEAR, RACE trials will refine further


### Esophageal SCC (ESCC)

- **Standard of care:** nCRT followed by surgery remains preferred option
- Adjuvant checkpoint inhibition in **residual disease** is the best augmentation
- Docetaxel-based nCT is a **viable regional alternative**
- Selective omission of surgery after induction CRT — on the horizon


### Shared Principles

- Chemotherapy or chemoradiotherapy **must** precede surgery in locally advanced disease
- nCRT achieves superior **locoregional control**, especially in ESCC
- nCT provides superior **systemic disease control** — pCR after nCT predicts better OS than pCR after nCRT
- Significant **regional practice variation** exists globally
- **Immunotherapy** integration — promising pathological responses; survival data pending

**Emerging frontier:** Selective surgery after induction chemoradiation for both ESCC and EAC — future trials may enable definitive non-surgical management in select patients.





## Key Take-Home Points

::: {.incremental}

- **nRT alone** is not a standard of care — only palliative utility
- **nCRT** (CROSS regimen: carboplatin + paclitaxel + 41.4 Gy) is an established Western standard for both EAC and ESCC
- **ESCC** shows superior pCR (49%) and survival with nCRT vs EAC (25%)
- **nCT** (FLOT) is the preferred approach for EAC — especially when combined with transthoracic en bloc surgery
- **pCR** after nCT predicts better survival than pCR after nCRT — systemic control matters more than locoregional control in EAC
- **ESCC:** both nCT and nCRT are acceptable standards; nCRT improves local control but overall survival is equivalent
- **Docetaxel-based triplet nCT (DCF/FLOT)** has superseded older doublet regimens
- **Immunotherapy** shows promise in increasing pathological response rates; survival benefit yet to be confirmed
- **Surgery approach matters:** en bloc transthoracic esophagectomy may reduce the added benefit of nCRT by providing superior locoregional control independently

:::
